questions.prompt: Per the syllabus, the final exam is:

choices.A: In-class on the last day, Oct 14
choices.B: A take-home due during exam week
choices.C: Friday, Oct 16, 5:30–8:30 pm, Evans Hall 4400/4410, all sections

questions.prompt: Per the syllabus, which statement about AI use in this course is TRUE?

choices.B: AI is required on PS2, but every number you submit must be one you can reproduce and defend — and the final is closed-book without AI
choices.C: AI is optional on everything including the final
choices.D: AI may be used only for writing memos

questions.prompt: A startup spends $180K per month on operating costs and collects $60K per month in cash from customers. Its **net burn** is:
The same startup has $1,440,000 in the bank. Its runway is approximately:
Booked (invoiced) revenue that has NOT yet been collected in cash:

choices.B: Does not reduce net burn — only cash collections do

questions.prompt: Research on U.S. private firms (Lisowsky & Minnis) shows that most large private companies:

choices.A: Are audited because the law requires it
choices.B: Carry NO audited financial statements — audits are bought when investors, lenders, or big customers demand them
choices.C: Follow the same reporting rules as public firms

questions.prompt: A two-year-old startup keeps cash-basis books. What most typically forces the switch to accrual accounting?

choices.C: Outside counterparties — a VC round, a lender, or a large customer demanding GAAP-style statements

questions.prompt: In the assigned a16z podcast, the CFO's most fundamental job is described as knowing:

choices.A: The company's valuation at all times
choices.B: The cash position and how many months of runway remain

questions.prompt: An investor puts $2M into a company at a $6M pre-money valuation. The post-money valuation is:
In Q1, what percentage of the company does the new investor own after the round?
An angel offers "$1.5M for 30% of the company." What post-money valuation did she just quote?
The company closes the seed round. What does the accountant record?

choices.B: Only the cash invested: Dr Cash / Cr Preferred Stock

questions.prompt: New shares for a round are computed as Z = S₀ ÷ (1 − x) rather than S₀ × (1 + x) because:

choices.A: The new shares are a fraction of the POST-round total, which includes themselves — the (1−x) trick solves the circularity

questions.prompt: A term sheet requires a 15% option pool created BEFORE the round (carved from the pre-money). Who is diluted by the pool?

choices.B: The existing holders (founders and earlier investors) — the new investor's percentage is protected

questions.prompt: The journal entry when the option pool is created at closing is:

choices.C: No entry — creating a pool authorizes shares; expense starts only as granted options are earned
choices.D: A memo entry at fair value

questions.prompt: "Fully diluted shares" counts:

choices.B: Outstanding shares plus everything convertible into shares — granted options, warrants, and the unallocated pool

questions.prompt: "Double taxation" of a C-corp means:

choices.A: The corporate rate is twice the personal rate
choices.B: Profits are taxed once at the corporate level and again at the shareholder level when distributed as dividends or realized as gains

questions.prompt: The general after-tax rule: choose a pass-through over a C-corp when:
One business earns $100 pre-tax and distributes everything this year. Rates: ordinary 30%, corporate 20%, shareholder 20%. The owner's after-tax cash is:

choices.A: LLC $70 vs. C-corp $60 — LLC wins by $10
choices.B: LLC $70 vs. C-corp $64 — LLC wins by $6

questions.prompt: Under the post-July-2025 QSBS rules, stock newly issued today qualifies for exclusion caps and holding tiers of:

choices.B: Greater of $15M or 10× basis; 50%/75%/100% exclusion at 3/4/5 years

questions.prompt: Your LLC allocates you $2M of taxable income but distributes $0 cash. On your personal return you owe tax on:

choices.A: The full $2M allocated — phantom income; CFOs negotiate tax distributions in the operating agreement

questions.prompt: VCs insist portfolio companies be Delaware C-corps mainly because:

choices.B: Standardized preferred stock, no K-1s/UBTI for their tax-exempt LPs, QSBS access, and clean option plans
choices.C: C-corps pay lower rates than LLCs

questions.prompt: The IRS decides employee-vs-contractor status primarily on:

choices.C: Control factors — behavioral control, financial control, and the nature of the relationship

questions.prompt: Your "Operations Manager" earns a $40K salary and mostly staffs the register. For overtime purposes she is:

choices.A: Exempt — she has a manager title
choices.C: Non-exempt — the FLSA duties test governs; title and salary form alone don't
choices.D: Exempt if she agrees in writing

questions.prompt: An employee receives restricted stock vesting over 4 years and files NO 83(b) election. She recognizes ordinary income:

choices.A: At each vest date, on that tranche's fair market value
choices.D: Never — it converts to capital gain

questions.prompt: The 83(b) election must be filed within:

choices.C: 30 days of GRANT — no extensions, no exceptions

questions.prompt: Which award is INELIGIBLE for an 83(b) election?

choices.C: RSUs — no property transfers at grant, so there is nothing to elect on

questions.prompt: Under ASC 718, the option expense a company books each year equals:

choices.A: Grant-date fair value ÷ vesting years — never remeasured as the stock moves
choices.B: The intrinsic value at each year-end

questions.prompt: Who can legally receive an INCENTIVE stock option (ISO)?

choices.C: Employees only — a consultant's "ISO" is necessarily an NQSO

questions.prompt: An employee exercises ISOs and HOLDS the shares. In that year, the bargain element (FMV − strike) is:

choices.C: Not regular taxable income — but it IS an AMT preference add-back

questions.prompt: FreshBites' Series A preferred sold at $4.00; its 409A values common at $2.03. The gap mainly reflects:

choices.A: The valuation firm lowballing to help employees
choices.B: The preferred's liquidation preference plus marketability/control discounts on common

questions.prompt: A company grants options struck BELOW the current 409A fair market value of common. The consequence is:

choices.B: §409A penalties — immediate income plus a 20% penalty tax on the employee, and payroll/withholding exposure for the company

questions.prompt: The annual operating plan (AOP), once approved by the board:

choices.A: Does not change during the year — it is the fixed benchmark; the monthly FORECAST is where updated truth lives

questions.prompt: A ROLLING forecast differs from a monthly re-forecast of the current fiscal year because it:

choices.B: Always extends a constant horizon (e.g., 12 months forward), adding a new period as each one closes, rather than shrinking toward Dec 31

questions.prompt: "Driver-based planning" means:

choices.A: Budgeting the controllable activities (impressions, CTR, conversion, hires) that produce the financials, rather than typing line-item dollar targets
choices.B: Letting department heads set their own budgets

questions.prompt: A company spends $300,000 on sales & marketing in a quarter and acquires 600 new customers. CAC is:
Gross revenue churn differs from net revenue churn because net churn:

choices.B: Offsets churned and contracted revenue with EXPANSION revenue from surviving customers — so it can be negative

questions.prompt: A company keeps 94% of its LOGOS but reports 108% net revenue retention. This happens when:

choices.A: Small customers churn while surviving (larger) customers expand by more than the lost revenue
choices.C: New sales are included in NRR

questions.prompt: Which set of inputs is sufficient for a standard LTV calculation?

choices.B: Average revenue per customer, gross margin, and a retention/churn rate (expected customer lifetime)

questions.prompt: The classic health benchmarks for a SaaS business are:
Per the Ground Rules, who is allowed to touch the Excel workbook?

choices.A: Only you — the AI never receives or edits the .xlsx; it works by paste-in/paste-out
choices.C: Either, if you check its work

questions.prompt: The AI cites "median Series-A logo churn: 0.8%/month (SaaS Capital, 2025)" and you cannot trace it to the benchmark sheet or a checkable source. You must:

choices.B: Stamp it UNVERIFIED in your table and verification log; authority-sounding is not sourced
choices.D: Average it with your own guess

questions.prompt: The AI's driver table lists "annual price increase: 5%" but the case never states one. That number is:

choices.A: An invention — log it, strike it, and convert it to an OPEN QUESTION for management

questions.prompt: The four AI roles you will run today are:
Every AI claim you rely on must appear in the verification log as:

choices.A: Prompt → claim → check performed → result (confirmed/corrected/rejected) → change made to the model

questions.prompt: From your `case_facts.txt` skim: Redline Labs sells:

choices.B: An AI contract-review copilot to mid-market law firms — $2,500/month platform fee plus $2 per document above a 1,000-document monthly allowance

questions.prompt: Why does today's Prompt 3 FORBID the AI from emitting cell formulas?

choices.B: You must own and be able to audit every cell — a model built by the AI is a model you cannot defend
choices.C: Formulas are too slow to paste

questions.prompt: Logistics check — my group has confirmed for Monday:

choices.A: A laptop with desktop Excel + charger, and at least one working LLM login (free tier fine)
choices.C: Login but no desktop Excel (Numbers/web only)

questions.prompt: A customer signs a 3-year, $360K contract today; nothing is invoiced or delivered yet. Right now the company has:
MRR and ARR exclude:

choices.B: One-time fees (activation, setup, services) — those live in ACV and TCV

questions.prompt: Billings for a period equal:

choices.A: Revenue + the change in deferred revenue

questions.prompt: Step 1 of ASC 606 requires a contract where collectability is PROBABLE. If your customer likely cannot pay, you:

choices.A: Book revenue and reserve for bad debt
choices.B: Do not recognize revenue at all — the model never starts

questions.prompt: A customer prepays $120K for a 12-month service. After 3 months, the balance sheet shows deferred revenue of:
A platform collects $100 from a buyer and remits $80 to the third-party seller who owes the fulfillment. As an AGENT, the platform's revenue is:

choices.B: $20 — the fee it keeps; amounts collected for others are excluded

questions.prompt: A pure SaaS subscription (vendor hosts; customer has a right to access, never owns the software) is recognized:
Under ASC 606, a sales commission paid up front on a multi-year contract is:

choices.B: Capitalized as an incremental cost of obtaining the contract and amortized over the benefit period

questions.prompt: A director appointed by the Series B fund legally owes fiduciary duties to:

choices.A: The Series B fund that appointed her
choices.B: ALL shareholders — care, candor, and loyalty run to the corporation and every holder, not the appointing class

questions.prompt: Per Sequoia and Feld, the board deck should be sent to directors:

choices.B: Days in advance — the meeting is for discussion and decisions, not for reading the update aloud

questions.prompt: The ONE number a burning startup's board package must always show is:

choices.C: Cash, net burn, and months of runway — versus plan

questions.prompt: "Executive session" at the end of a board meeting means:

choices.A: The board meets without management — the CFO (and then the CEO) leave the room

questions.prompt: A VC-backed company most commonly gets its FIRST audit because:

choices.B: A term-sheet covenant or lender/exit requirement demands audited financials (typically around the ~$10M-revenue stage)

questions.prompt: A "PBC list" in an audit is:

choices.A: The Prepared-by-Client list — schedules and reconciliations the company must deliver to the auditors
choices.C: The board's questions for the auditor

questions.prompt: Board governance intensity should scale with:

choices.B: The gap between who OWNS the company and who CONTROLS it — near-zero at a 100% PE-owned company, wide at a VC-backed founder-run company

questions.prompt: Observer seats are limited and negotiated because observers:

choices.B: See confidential material and exert creeping influence WITHOUT fiduciary accountability — plus leak and efficiency risk

questions.prompt: "2 and 20" fund economics means the GPs earn:

choices.A: A ~2% annual management fee on committed capital plus 20% carried interest on profits

questions.prompt: A typical VC fund has a life of ~10 years with new investments made mostly in the first ~5. A fund in YEAR 8 that led your Series B will predictably:

choices.B: Push toward liquidity — exits or secondaries — because its clock is running out

questions.prompt: An investor holds $4M of 1× NON-participating preferred bought for 20% of the company. The company sells for $12M. The investor receives:
PARTICIPATING preferred differs because the holder:

choices.A: Takes the preference AND THEN shares pro rata in the remainder — the "double dip," with no conversion choice to make

questions.prompt: On the balance sheet, a SAFE sits in:

choices.A: The equity section — it is a warrant-like agreement for future equity with no maturity or interest
choices.C: Long-term debt, like a convertible note

questions.prompt: Four SAFEs are outstanding and the founder says "our cap table is clean." The correct CFO response:

choices.B: The cap table LOOKS clean only because the SAFEs aren't on it yet; conversion at the next priced round will stack the dilution — model it now

questions.prompt: A venture-debt term sheet includes "10% warrant coverage" on a $3M loan. That means:

choices.A: The lender also gets warrants to buy ~$300K worth of stock — a dilution cost on top of the interest rate

questions.prompt: "Protective provisions" in a term sheet are:

choices.A: Economic terms — they set the price
choices.B: CONTROL terms — a veto list (sale of the company, new financings, budgets) that decides who can block what

questions.prompt: Private-company acquisitions are typically priced "cash-free, debt-free" because:

choices.A: Cash and funded debt are financing choices, not operating assets — the buyer prices the enterprise and the seller keeps/settles its own financing

questions.prompt: The working-capital PEG exists to:

choices.B: Stop the seller from stripping working capital (collecting AR hard, stretching payables, running down inventory) before close — the true-up adjusts price dollar-for-dollar

questions.prompt: Peg = $2.0M. At closing, properly adjusted NWC delivered is $1.6M. Dollar-for-dollar, the buyer:

choices.C: Pays the same — pegs only move escrow

questions.prompt: A seller's CFO should resist an EBITDA-based earn-out because:

choices.A: Post-close the BUYER controls costs and allocations — EBITDA is gameable against the seller; prefer revenue metrics, defined policies, and audit rights
choices.B: EBITDA is too easy to hit

questions.prompt: PE buyers usually want management to ROLL part of their equity into the new deal because:

choices.A: It aligns incentives and signals confidence (and reduces sponsor cash) — management gets a "second bite of the apple"

questions.prompt: A C-corp seller comparing a $40M stock sale to a $41M asset sale should remember that the ASSET sale:

choices.A: Triggers corporate-level tax on the gain AND shareholder-level tax on distribution — the extra $1M rarely covers the second layer

questions.prompt: Signing a letter of intent (LOI) typically changes the process because:

choices.A: Exclusivity begins — the seller stops shopping while the buyer runs serious diligence, and leverage tilts to the buyer

questions.prompt: Ball & Shivakumar's evidence on IPO-year reporting shows that, on average, IPO firms:

choices.B: Report MORE conservatively — the monitoring stack (auditors, underwriters, analysts, litigation risk) disciplines them
